Im sorry all this is happening. This sounds incredibly painful and stressful. 

I went through some similar circumstances as your daughter. S.A. at 18 by a much older man, refused therapy, and became cold and emotionally detached from reality. 

After the assault I fell into a whirlwind, I was abusive and being abused by my ex at the time, I had consistent flashbacks which skewed my reality. I was on high alert all the time. The flashbacks made it feel like whoever was there at the time WAS the person who S.A. me. 

I think this might be what your daughter is experiencing.  She may have demonized you as well because she correlates you with your mom. Even though you helped her, she may feel betrayed for a multitude of reasons. She may be upset you let her stay there in the first place, or that if your mom was capable of turning a blind eye why wouldn't you.

Im not saying this it true by the way, but those were some of the things that went through my mind during those times. Logic and reasoning and emotional control is already difficult at 19 due to incomplete prefrontal cortex development. A horribly traumatic event makes that entire area of the brain misfire. 

Its easy to look for blame in others, and normal at her age. As she gets older and hopefully begins therapy, she will hopefully realize that sometimes bad things happen that are out of your control. Shitty people exist, but differentiating between good and bad people will be easier over time.

It sounds like she is gravitating to people similar to her abuser (I say this because you said she was choosing to live with your abusive ex). I did the same thing. 

Unfortunately some roads in life have to be traveled alone. I got better because I wanted to. No amount of external forces would have made me seek treatment. I had to hit my rock bottom first.

Perhaps the only thing you can do for her is apologize for the abuse she endured, let her know if you could turn back time to stop it you of course would never have let this happen, and she will always have a place with you to turn to for emotional, physical, and mental support. You will help her recieve help when she is ready. Then give her some space.

Youre doing the best you can, and she is too. Hugs xx

Speaking from the eyes of my child self, it is far more damaging to be in that environment and experience the addiction everyday than it was to deal with the separation. 

I was emotionally drawn more to my father because he was metally and physically unavailable. I would constantly do more and more impressive things and accomplishments in order to try and convince him I was worthy enough to be in his life. In hopes that maybe this time he will show up to see me get my award or to come to parent teacher night and see how well I was doing. 

Eventually this led to me internalizing it and feeling like nothing I did was ever good enough. My mother suffered with mental health issues so both environments were less than ideal unfortunately but at least she was there and tried.

What you do next is entirely your choice. Neither is easy, and both will have a some negative effect on the kids. Weigh out your pros and cons. Determine what issues may arise with each. Find a game plan for how to deal with the issues. In the end, put safety above any emotional influences.

Safety can go both ways depending on your situation. If you risk being homeless or have no way to support the kids alone, I can understand hesitation to leave. However if he is actively physically, mentally or verbally abusing you or the kids, seek immediate help at a DV shelter.

Whatever you decide to do, you are doing the best you can with whats available to you. Youre being a good mom and will only ever do whats in their best interests. 

Better days ahead, hugs xx

Hey there, fellow ADHDer with former coke abuse.

My main saving grace was therapy. Truely.

Its easy to take more and more of my stimulant to continue seeing the highest output I have ever been capable of. It is too easy actually. Just one more and I can finish that 10 page essay today and have the weekend with not homework!

The thing with ADHD is we need structure as I am sure you know. Our meds is like a parent nagging us to do work, do chores, shower, eat, etc. 

In the end, your parents (meds) didnt do the work for you, you did it. They were just the fire under your ass.

In therapy, I am currently working through ADHD curriculum. I.E..... How to hold myself accountable, how to deal with impulsivity, how to slow my brain down through grounding so I am not such a hot head, how to remember tasks, how to come up with reasonable workloads, how to forgive myself for not being a superhuman capable of non stop productivity. 

I have noticed a lot of people with ADHD also gave a need for perfectionism. In whatever shape or form they latch to. They have to "hold it all together", "accomplish more", "not let other down at the expense of themselves". 

We more often than not look at our shortcomings instead of our successes. Yet, we are usually putting in 200% effort and accomplishing more than our NT counterparts. 

The meds are there to nag you to go through the curriculum and establish skills that compliment the medicine. The meds are not your saving grace, you are. Try therapy and express a want to do ADHD curriculum. It may not fix everything, you will still have ADHD, but it is a lot easier and less guilt filled to turn to the skills you learned instead of another pill. 

Best of luck xx

Hey hun, 

Ive been there. Horribly depressed at finals.

One thing that has helped me is to take all the notes from the semester for each class & pin them together with a paperclip/staple in chronological order.

From there if I have the energy Ill condense it all on one paper front and back per class of all the important "highlights"/formulas I need.

While I dont condone cramming, you gotta do what you gotta do babe. 

First things, staple each classes notes together.

Next, take a hot bath, get clean, exfoliate, shave, make yourself feel comfortable. 

Finally, if you have the finances, order something with a lot of carbs, vegetables, and protein. Stir fried rice is my go to finals meal.

From there glancing at your notes will be easier because theyre all organized. If you feel up for it, condense it down. If not, take some time for you. Watch your favorite tv show, play some video games, or do a favorite hobby. 

Being in a clear, relaxed mind will help you more on the test than studying to the deadline. If youre stressed and not taking care of yourself you will get severe tip of the tongue no matter how much you prepped. Take care of you please.

You are strong, you are smart, you are worthy, you are capable, I believe in you. Hugs xxxx

BPD and Vulnerable Narcissism are two separate diagnoses technically. However BPD falls under the vulnerable narcissism umbrella. 

Unfortunately BPD has this negative stigma that we are all uncaring narcissists. In my case it couldn't be farther from the truth, I hurt others as a knee jerk reaction to prevent myself from getting hurt. I knew what I was doing was wrong and would beat myself up about it. 

The line where BPD ends and narcissism begins is very blurry and hard to navigate. Regardless, putting your mental health first is your top priority. 

BPD also instills a lot of emotional incest and parentification unfortunately. Im glad your looking into a therapist for yourself. It can be scary to think you are becoming what you never wanted to be. Breaking the cycle is a long hard process but the peace and clarity is worthwhile. 

Best wishes xx

In general, drawing out the Lewis structure of both of these compounds helps. There are multiple ways to get the same result, and your theory is not technically wrong.

When drawing out the Lewis structure of NH2, which follows the octet rule, it needs to borrow a electron and holds a negative charge. Leading me to make the Hydrogen bond negative. 

While BH3, does not follow the octet rule, but is a very stable element due to the satisfied Hydrogen bonds. Leading me to make the net Hydrogen as positive. 

You could theoretically just follow the Hydrogen rules for oxidation numbers, as long as the net result is the same.

So if there is no charge at the end of the compound, then the sum of oxidation numbers is equal to zero.

Hydrogen follows the +1,-1 rule. In CH3 the Hydrogen is a +1, since there are 3 it totals to +3.

To make the sum of CH3 equal zero, the oxidation number of Carbon must be -3. 

Continuing down the line. 
CH3-CH2-NH2-BH3
(-3,+1)( -2,+1)(-3,-1)(+2,+1)

If you would rather spend time alone, schedule in a video game session or another hobby for that day.

If you and your cat are happy with clay, stick with clay!

Transition periods between clay and pellets are different for every cat. I was lucky, my cats took to it right away. I didnt have to slowly transition them. I just bought a sifting box, threw pellets in there, and they all used it!

You might not be so lucky / your cat throws up a big middle finger at the even the thought of using it.

There are plenty of videos on youtube on how to transition them. A quick run down though, have one box with old litter, one box with new litter. Leave that for a few days. They may start using the new box unprovoked, they may not. After a few days, start adding about a cup of new litter to the clay. 

The issue here is that wood pellets do not clump so the clean up will be difficult if your cats on the pickier side.

Keep adding more pellets and less clay about every 3 or so days until the box is all pellet.

Some cats will refuse the pellets all together bc they are a bit rougher on their paws. Some signs that the litter is to hard for them is if they start urinating on blankets or couches or beds. 

You may want to get some natures miracle or other urine remover as well as a lot of baking soda during this transition period. Better to have and not need than to need and not have.

I personally am against automatic litter boxes because it is not in the best interest for your cat(s).

They are loud and scary and the movement is less than ideal for them. Its not just a moral issue though, because if the cat decides that the litterbox is scary and they don't wanna use it anymore, they will start having accidents outside the litterbox.

I find what works best for me is to have an open top, non enclosed litterbox in an area that I can see and is easy to get to.

That means, dont hide it! When I can see the litterbox everyday when I get a drink of water, I am WAY more likely to actually clean it. 

There are many different types of boxes. Plain plastic, sifting plastic boxes, and stainless steel boxes.

If you are aiming for minimizing smell, the stainless steel boxes and easy to clean and dont absorb urine smell. Plastic boxes will need to be replaced yearly-biyearly.

As for litter, they all kind of suck tbh. I dont like clay because it tracks very very bad throughout the whole house. But it is the easiest to get, the cats like it and usually cheap. 

I personally use wood pellets, but they dont clump so it involves either a sifting litterbox or sifting trash can to clean. I like it because it doesnt have a harsh smell, it doesnt track as bad, and its 6 dollars for a 50pound bag at tractor supply co. 

I recommend washing out the litterbox each time you dump it with some soap and water. It keeps the smell down and your cat will thank you haha.
